expectedFacts: TransactionContextPooled.__aenter__ acquires a pool connection and then calls get_connections().set(connection_name, client) to install the transaction client before begin().

ConnectionHandler.set copies the alias-to-client dict, puts the transaction client in the copy and stores it in a ContextVar, so the replacement is visible only to the current asyncio task; it returns a token.

When no explicit connection or router choice applies, a plain query falls back to the model's MetaInfo.db property, which calls get_connection(default_connection) -> ConnectionHandler.get; that reads the same ContextVar storage and so returns the transaction client.
TransactionContextPooled.__aexit__ commits or rolls back and, in a finally block, calls get_connections().reset(token) to restore the previous storage.

r3-tortoise-orm-08.query: When a brand-new instance is saved through the default PostgreSQL driver and the database assigns its auto-incrementing primary key, how does that database-assigned value get back onto the Python object?

expectedFacts: DatetimeField.to_db_value emits a RuntimeWarning saying the field received a naive datetime while time zone support is active.
It then converts the value with timezone.make_aware (using the configured default timezone) and validates it, so the aware value is what is written.

r3-tortoise-orm-20.query: Where is it enforced that a brand-new object cannot be constructed pointing at a related object that has not been stored yet, and is the same rule applied when the relation is later set by plain attribute assignment?

expectedFacts: BulkCreateQuery._analyze_db_default_fields scans every instance for each db_default column: values that are DatabaseDefault sentinels count as 'default', anything else as 'explicit'.
If one column has both kinds it raises OperationalError explaining the options (set everywhere, omit everywhere, or split the call).

If every instance relies on the default, the column is added to the returned omit set; both callers (__await__ and sql()) pass that set to _make_queries so the column is left out of the INSERT and the database default applies.

There is no soft-delete support: Model.delete issues a real DELETE through executor.execute_delete, and the default Manager.get_queryset returns an unfiltered QuerySet (a user may supply a custom Meta.manager that filters, but the library sets no deleted marker).
No deleted flag, timestamp or default filtering exists anywhere in the package.
